paragraph: Fairview runs on two-families. Thirteen multi-family sales in six months at a median of $800,000, almost all of them two-family houses with around six bedrooms across the units, and a 1.03 sale-to-list ratio with more than three quarters closing above list. Median days on market is 22, so this is competitive without being frenzied, and buyers should expect competition on the good ones. Detached single-family is thin by comparison at six sales, median $645,000, mostly four-bedroom colonials with two baths, and the sale-to-list ratio of 1.01 with half going above asking says the same thing: priced right, it moves in about three weeks. Condos and townhouses are the softer tier, nine sales at a median of $545,000 against a $574,900 median list, a 0.98 ratio, and 34 days on market. That is the one place you'll find real negotiating room, and the range from $279,000 to $780,000 is wide enough that the median is the number to anchor on. Monthly closings here are too thin to read a trend from, one to three sales a month, so the six-month picture is the honest guide. If you're comparing tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space of a single-family, the rental income of a two-family, or the low-maintenance lifestyle of a condo.
